english: You see a collection of books from the philosophy canon none of which you are really able to understand.
Next to them, a line of famous political books. Azgalist theory, Hedonists, the Dark Book of Shadow, Léxandro. Many more.
Hm. No Freestrider work. Disappointing.
This scholar has good taste.
You approach the complicated books once more.
(Open, 'The Folk' by Léxandro.)
(Open, 'A Blind Manifesto' by the Hedonists.)
(Open, 'Memoirs of a Statesman' by Nicholas Darrow.)
E-I'm done here.
Léxandro.
This was the first book placed in your hands as an Urthfolk recruit.
Open it.
(Look inside.)
(Put it back.)
It's an old, worn copy of that same text.
Musings about the Divine Era. Of great walking gods and their theocratic states.
A history lesson, morphing into a series of guidelines: how modern leaders, as a response to the drawn-out Coast War, should return to the old.
The proven. The organized.
The divine.
Although written from the perspective of not faith nor service to the holy, but rather that of service to the state.
A modern theocratic vision. The nation as an entity not bound by the protection and lifetime of its god.
Instead, the nation state will survive on unifying cultural traits, passed down from that god to his people.
This, Léxandro writes, will fasten them into the earth, creating firm groundings for the states to exist beyond any others.
The later chapters go on to describe his dream of a Millennium Empire. His grand plan. A nation to survive the passing of eras.
A collection of ideas he gathers in this dream. An ideology, structured around order, without the weakness of monarchy, the chaos of democracy, or the esoteric dependence of magocracy.
The Millennium Empire. The FASCIST ideal.
A good book. Léxandro knew what he was talking about.
It's almost like he wrote directly about the struggles of today's Norvik.
Dangerous ideas. Fascism has led many cities astray in Reeds.
I don't care about this.
Whatever your thoughts are, this book is used to reshape the city.
You live in fear of where its path will lead.
You know well how effective it is.
Just remember: it was written by a gnome.
Léxandro was a gnome. He tried using the so-called Fasci di Condottieri, the great mercenary warlords of Old Diminor, to bring order to the neglected parts of the Band.
He was, however, ultimately destroyed by the same warlords he created, when his followers failed in their coup of Savalni.
Ironically, the responsible squad reportedly did not realize who they had killed at first - they had simply been hunting down any non-humans in the city.
This... this was not openly spoken about during your training.
But yes. It is true.
Something to ponder.
His followers misunderstood his message, then.
That is indeed, very ironic.
(Put the book away.)
If a message is misconstrued - is that the fault of the reader or the writer?
The reader.
The writer.
I don't know.
Both.
Yes.
It is both.
Indeed it is.
You close it, and place it back in its spot.
Perhaps later, then.
The book.
THE book.
Always listen to your hungry stomach, it says with big, ugly letters on the first page.
You should listen to the book. And the stomach.
This crazy old text...
This wonderful manual...
This foul debauchery...
Same as always, the book begins with a tirade about property ownership.
Then, on the fifth page, you find a diagram showing how to ritualistically summon a demon.
It's incorrect however. On purpose, supposedly.
The purpose is metaphoric criticism of authoritarian governments.
The rest is a series of extreme essays on the topics of Hedonism: rejection of statehood, free association, maximizing sensation, direct democracy, and reciprocal exchange.
It paints up an image of an ideal world, where all can live without strife simply through the cooperation and love of all things.
A loving image. Communally loving.
Made illegal in many cities after its release in 466 AE, this rambling text has survived for one reason or another.
It is... the <shake>thing</shake> that makes you feel good.
The text of TRUTH.
(Look at the chapter on 'free love'.)
You flip to pages fifty-two. You remember it well.
It. Has. <shake>Pictures</shake>.
Tiny scribbling. Something akin to stick figures, positioned in various enwrapped unities.
You remember the words well. The guide on how to 'make ultimate sensations of flesh'.
Kinda hot. In a sad way.
Remember it well.
You will need it one day.
Close the book.
Reading filth like this will only darken your mind.
The Hedonists are back on the shelf.
The Coinlord's own book.

The first few pages are devoted to a rambling text about the history of governing. From ancient texts from various Beasts of Jor, to gods of the Divine Era, to several Arcanist figures- Darrow then smoothly moves on to conflate their accomplishments with his own.
Especially since he also includes an explanation of his lineage- that he is a direct first-born grandson of Borgo Darrow, the first paladin of Urth.
It is not-so subtle.
The many, many pages go on to describe both practical but mostly theoretical methods a 'statesman' should use when dealing with the populace, the bureaucracy, and the ideologies of modern life.
You haven't read this before.
Luckily, you don't have time to do so now either.

Generally, the book has a rather rough tone about democracy. A quote you've heard before from this book pops up towards the end: Those who believe in democracy have a wonderful view of folk - to think them capable of making rational and informed decisions devoid of personal bias and emotional conduct.
From what you remember, it caused quite the stir when it came out two years ago.
Quite anti-democratic.
No wonder people were upset. To have a Magistrate use such terrible language...
You recall a rumor about Shieldlord Jarn having hated this book so much during its printing that he personally bought two hundred copies only to burn them in his garden.
It's probably not true. Probably.
You do so.
You pick up the black-covered tome. A faint tingle goes through your gloved hand.
That's the most evil book I've ever seen.
How'd they even get the cover to be THAT black?
It's like a void.
Thicken graphene.
That is how they create the darkness on the cover.
A memory lingers in this tome.
If you open it, you shall recall.
R-(Open it, despite its evil nature.)
The text is not dangerous. The pages show but a holy scripture of the Shadow Lord's lost religion. One of eternal servitude and the search for life in death.
However.
You remember it well.
This was the first book you were ordered to study, as punishment for your idiotic behavior at the Towers.
You remember.
Your first journey towards the esoteric.
Recall it.
No, I shouldn't.
How liberating it was.
To know, beyond any doubt, how much greatness hid within your mind.
How painful it was.
To know, beyond any doubt, how alone you truly are.
Fine.
Stay ignorant.
Hm. Fine.
Blurred faces. Hushed whispers.
A crowd of thoughtful peers, each snickering about your hand.
A raised hand. Among a crowd of sheep.
Patriarch. It's not just a religious text.
They stare at you.
It's a spellbook.
Those were the words.
Oh, how they laughed.
He asked you to prove yourself.
So you did.
I went up to the Patriarch. I took the Book of Shadow...
Then I...
Yes.
(Memorize Detect Alignment.)

You memorized it on the spot. Then you cast that ancient spell, once used by the Death Knights of the Shadow Lord to subjugate and control the minds of his people. A spell that is, despite its first level, not learned by most clerics until they grasp the intricacies of higher tier casting.
Everyone was left stunned by your excellence.
They should have clapped.
To not only master such a spell, but to do it in seconds instead of days...
That moment- it was yours.
From that moment you marked your place at the Towers as the greatest spellcaster, the greatest talent, among them all.
However, as always, the weak fear the strong.
That moment also began your ostracization.
You would never be among them. Never have peers. None would see you in any way as a brother or a comrade.
I would be a leader.
I would be an enemy.
I would be an obstacle.
I would be their end.
You are.
And you shall continue to be.
(Gasp for air.)
Your vision is blurry.
It is filled by the pages of that book.
It is a good one, despite its religious fervor.
As many say- the Shadow Lord was as much an early Arcanist as he was the greatest of the walking gods.
(Close the book.)
